printed.Positions and times: July 2 attached to Webb's brigade, engaged Wright's Georgians in late afternoon. July 3 morning: enemy fire exploded three limbers (Hazard). Just below the crest between the 71st and 72nd Pa; limbers second line, caissons third. Fire knocked out four of six guns; Webb allowed the guns to be run to the wall; double canister at about 100 yd; Cushing killed at the last shot.
printed.Losses: Monument: 38 casualties (1 officer and 5 men killed; 1 officer and 31 men wounded); all but one gun and all but three horses disabled. Canby wounded; every officer killed or wounded
printed.Sources and conflicts: Warfare History Network; Stone Sentinels; Iron Brigader

printed.Positions and times: Arrived 9 am July 2; four guns above Devil's Den at 2 pm; one section shifted right near Winslow about 6 pm. Two guns in the Plum Run valley fired canister at Benning's brigade; four on the ridge; when ordered back, valley guns and one ridge gun got away; three ridge guns captured and given to Henry's battalion.

Marched about 4:30 pm July 2 to the rear of Barnes's division; opened fire 5:45 pm; fired until after dark; July 3 remained and supported against Longstreet's assault. One gun driven to the summit; the rest effectively carried up; ammunition run up from caissons below. Hazlett mortally wounded kneeling by Weed; Rittenhouse took command.
printed.Losses: 1 officer and 8 men killed, 5 wounded (14 total)
printed.Sources and conflicts: Stone Sentinels; Civil War in the East

printed.Rounds: 850 total; 200 lost with a broken caisson
printed.Losses: revised to 8 wounded, 3 missing; 12 horses killed
printed.Sources and conflicts: 13th NY Battery site. Lost a gun when the prolonge broke on July 2

printed.Positions and times: Night June 30 in a hollow. July 1 morning: right and center sections about 600 yd from it. Roder (right), Newman (center), Pergel (left). Archer's brigade seen advancing about 1,000 yd away at about 9:55 am (estimate); left section pulled back because the woods came within 200 yd. Monument: first Union gun of the battle fired from the right section; held under severe fire until I Corps arrived about 10 am; relieved by Hall's 2nd Maine, resupplied, returned to a line in front of Cemetery Ridge; at night about a mile left near the III Corps. Buford's report: Calef "held his own gloriously" against 12 guns.
printed.Rounds: not stated; whether the battery ran short is a gap

cannonade_july3.printed_intro: Sequence and values, with every conflicting figure carried (sources: NPS Handbook 9, StrategyPage, American Battlefield Trust, HistoryNet, History Is Now, Wikipedia Pickett's Charge, CivilWarTalk quoting Hunt, Emerging Civil War, Hazard report):

rows.printed: About 1 pm; two guns near the Peach Orchard (Miller's battery) fired as the signal (NPS Handbook 9). HistoryNet says Whitworths on Oak Ridge fired the signal. Union gunners waited, then about 80 guns opened (NPS).
rows.conflict: signal guns: Miller's battery vs Whitworths on Oak Ridge

rows.printed: About a two-mile line (Trust, "around 150"). Cabell's guns near a small brick house; Carter's ten rifles at the railroad cut; Alexander's battalion with the assault; Hurt's Whitworths on Oak Hill.

138-179 estimates; Pendleton said nearly 150; Alexander's 179 included about two dozen howitzers held for the infantry; at least 142 shown to have fired; reasoned range 142-155 (StrategyPage). Other figures: 130-170 (Coddington over 150; Eicher 159; Trudeau 164; Clark and Pfanz about 170, per Wikipedia Pickett's Charge); 150-170 (HistoryNet, History Is Now); about 80 ANV guns unused (Wikipedia); a Confederate officer estimated about 300 total.

About 106 deployed on the ridge, about 85 engaged briefly, about 136 held in reserve (StrategyPage); as many as 120 on Cemetery Ridge and Hill (Trust); only about 80 available for counter-battery (History Is Now; Hunt per Wikipedia); 80 (NPS).
Nearly two hours (NPS; Cabell "over two hours"); about 1 1/4 hours at II Corps (Hazard); roughly one hour (History Is Now); one to two hours (HistoryNet); ended around 3 pm (Trust); Wheeler 1-3 pm.

At 10 am inspected batteries and told them to hold fire against small targets, to concentrate on one enemy battery when the Confederates opened, and to conserve ammunition; at noon described the Confederate line as covering the whole two-mile front (CivilWarTalk quoting Hunt's report; not read from the OR). After about two hours he ordered batteries to slow; withdrew damaged and low-ammunition batteries and prepared canister (Trust). Hunt pulled several batteries from the center so the Confederates would think they were destroyed and replaced them with reserve guns (Emerging Civil War).

Hancock countermanded the slowdown and ordered return fire; his officers answered they would obey their chief (Emerging Civil War; Trust). Hancock's anger is documented in secondary sources; the primary texts of both men were not read.

Alexander judged the Union fire weakening and his own ammunition low; sent word to Pickett (NPS Handbook). Another account: replenishing from trains would take over an hour, so the infantry advanced without close artillery support (History Is Now). Alexander's own report: batteries held positions through the afternoon of July 3. Exact ammunition figures are an open gap.
See B.6.14.2. Gunners aimed high to maximize shrapnel and smoke hung low in windless heat, so most shells flew into the Union rear (History Is Now).
Meade's HQ at the Leister house was made untenable by the bombardment and he moved to Powers Hill (HistoryNet). Meade-HQ casualties and horse losses are not retrieved.
Cushing's and Rorty's badly hurt; Osborn's guns on Cemetery Hill had a hard time (CivilWarTalk thread); three of Cushing's limbers exploded in the morning (Hazard).
McGilvery's batteries and Rittenhouse on Little Round Top described as the main fire disrupting Pickett's men (forum opinion).
Hunt's last four reserve batteries ordered up; he rode into the Angle and had his horse shot (Emerging Civil War). Fire shifted to canister within about 400 yd (Wikipedia Pickett's Charge).

animation_schedule.printed: Animation schedule (inferred; it fits the majority of sources; the two-hour duration seems to compress the whole artillery phase including the slowdown): 1:00 pm two-gun signal; about 30-40 minutes of full exchange; Union slowdown starting about 1:30-2:00 pm; Hunt/Hancock exchange; Union lull to about 2:45-3:00 pm; then Pickett's advance. Implementation: a randomized burst-distance error biased long (+150-200 yd) with a small rate of duds and early bursts for Confederate case and shell (plausible-procedural, seeded); many Confederate rounds burst beyond the ridge among limbers, caissons, horse lines and the Leister house vicinity, which explains rear-area carnage (inferred).

cannonade_july3.left_flank_sequence: Animation schedule driver (inferred): the Union left-flank sequence runs from about 2 pm (Smith at Devil's Den) through 4:00-4:30 (Hart, Bigelow, Phillips), 4:30-5:45 (Hazlett to Little Round Top) to about 6:30 (Bigelow overrun).

order_of_battle_notes: Notes and caveats (B.6.14.6): the Wikipedia page lists no battalion called "Lane" (Lane was an infantry brigadier in Pender's division), so Lane's artillery is not identifiable from sources. Allocating guns to Dearing, Eshleman, Alexander, Walker, Nelson, Garnett, Dance and others needs per-battery returns that were not found; use the 4-gun-per-battery default and the inventory in B.6.14.1 as a total check (inferred, plausible-procedural where applied). Henry's battalion arrived July 2; its July 3 positions were not retrieved (gap). Two sources differ on which batteries sat with which corps in the later phases (Alexander commanded the First Corps guns in the later phases of the battle).
